topic: Data Preprocessing: Handling Outliers, Missing Values, and Skewed Data

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: A Tier-1 digital payments platform processes over 15,000 transactions per second (TPS) and must classify fraudulent attempts within an end-to-end SLA of 20 milliseconds. The incoming streaming feature vector contains 180 continuous variables. Due to intermittent network timeouts at merchant POS terminals, approximately 8% of feature entries are Missing at Random (MAR). The current offline pipeline used MissForest (iterative random forest imputation) to achieve high predictive accuracy, but deploying this directly into the real-time inference microservice caused severe thread pool exhaustion and breached the SLA by exceeding 250ms per request.
questions.question: Which architectural decision provides the optimal trade-off between statistical fidelity, operational latency, and avoiding train-test data leakage?
options: A) Transition to K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Imputation using an approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) index stored in Redis cache to impute dynamically at inference time.
B) Deploy offline-computed median values alongside generated binary missingness indicator features, or utilize gradient boosted decision trees that treat missing values as a native split direction.
C) Implement a streaming Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) worker thread running parallel to the scoring engine to estimate missing values asynchronously.
D) Impute missing values dynamically using a deep autoencoder model deployed on a dedicated GPU cluster to reconstruct the corrupted input vector in sub-5ms.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Deploy offline-computed median values alongside generated binary missingness indicator features, or utilize gradient boosted decision trees that treat missing values as a native split direction.
questions.explanation: In production streaming systems with stringent latency budgets (<20ms), complex iterative imputation strategies like MICE, MissForest, or KNN are computationally prohibitive because their inference complexity scales with dataset dimensions and iterations ($O(M \cdot N \cdot D)$ or requires distance metrics across large reference sets). Tree-based algorithms (such as XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost) handle missing values natively during split finding by assigning missing values to whichever child node maximizes the split criterion (default direction determined during training), requiring zero imputation latency ($O(1)$ overhead). Alternatively, replacing missing values with offline-calculated static medians paired with binary missingness indicators preserves missingness pattern information without runtime computation bottlenecks or data leakage.

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: A credit scoring engine is being developed for an algorithmic lending platform using an ElasticNet generalized linear model. One of the strongest predictive features, 'Net Rolling Cashflow', exhibits extreme positive skewness (skewness index > 6.2) along with heavy right tails. Crucially, the feature contains exact zero values (dormant accounts) and negative values (overdrawn accounts with operational deficits). When attempting to normalize the distribution to satisfy linear model assumptions, the data science team encountered run-time math exceptions and degenerate outputs.
questions.question: Which data transformation method mathematically accommodates the negative and zero values while effectively stabilizing variance and rectifying the skewness towards normality?
options: A) Box-Cox transformation parameterized via maximum likelihood estimation after applying an arbitrary scalar shift ($x + |\min(x)| + 1$).
B) Standard Logarithmic transformation with increment $\log(x + 1)$ applied strictly to the absolute magnitude of the feature values.
C) Yeo-Johnson power transformation applied directly to the continuous feature without manual shifting.
D) Reciprocal transformation ($1 / x$) coupled with standard Min-Max scaling between 0 and 1.
questions.correct_answer_text: C) Yeo-Johnson power transformation applied directly to the continuous feature without manual shifting.
questions.explanation: The Box-Cox transformation is strictly defined only for strictly positive values ($x > 0$). While applying an arbitrary translation parameter ($x + c$) is sometimes attempted, it introduces an arbitrary hyperparameter that distorts variance and correlation structures. The Yeo-Johnson transformation extends the Box-Cox principle to support zero and negative values through a continuous piecewise power function: for $x \ge 0$, $\psi(\lambda, x) = ((x + 1)^\lambda - 1) / \lambda$ (for $\lambda \ne 0$), and for $x < 0$, $\psi(\lambda, x) = -((-x + 1)^{2 - \lambda} - 1) / (2 - \lambda)$ (for $\lambda \ne 2$). This stabilizes variance and reduces skewness across all real numbers without arbitrary shifting.

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: An IoT anomaly detection system monitors 220 high-frequency sensor streams from gas turbine engines. The feature space exhibits high dimensionality ($p = 220$) where true mechanical failure signatures manifest as sparse multivariate outliers. The engineering team initially deployed Mahalanobis Distance combined with a Chi-Square cut-off, but the system experienced mathematical breakdowns: the sample covariance matrix became ill-conditioned and singular during localized batch calculations. Furthermore, a secondary attempt using Euclidean distance-based Local Outlier Factor (LOF) failed due to distance concentration effects where distances between all pairs of points converged to nearly identical values.
questions.question: Which outlier detection strategy effectively circumvents both the distance concentration phenomenon of high-dimensional spaces and matrix inversion failure?
options: A) Isolation Forest relying on recursive random axis-aligned feature partitioning.
B) Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) with Moore-Penrose generalized pseudo-inversion.
C) Z-score standardization followed by feature-wise univariate Interquartile Range (IQR) filtering.
D) Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) calibrated with Manhattan distance metric.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Isolation Forest relying on recursive random axis-aligned feature partitioning.
questions.explanation: Distance-based metrics (like LOF, DBSCAN, and Euclidean distance) suffer in high dimensions from the 'curse of dimensionality', specifically the distance concentration phenomenon where $\lim_{d \to \infty} \frac{\text{dist}_{\max} - \text{dist}_{\min}}{\text{dist}_{\min}} \to 0$, rendering distance metrics discriminatively useless. Parametric elliptical methods like Mahalanobis Distance require computing the inverse covariance matrix $\Sigma^{-1}$, which becomes non-invertible/singular or numerically unstable when $p$ is large or collinearity is present. Isolation Forest does not calculate explicit distance metrics or covariance matrices; instead, it exploits the vulnerability of outliers to random axis-aligned recursive partitioning (anomalies require significantly fewer random splits to isolate and thus have noticeably shorter average path lengths in isolation trees).
